source.title: Reusing Space: Techniques and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Does the undirected s-t connectivity problem admit a simple, direct proof that it belongs to deterministic logspace L, preferably avoiding the heavier machinery used in existing proofs?

evidence.quote: Can reusing space be used to give a simpler, more efficient deterministic algorithm for uSTConn? ... Problem 1. Give a simple, direct proof of uSTConn ∈ L.

accepted.question_text: Does the undirected s-t connectivity problem admit a simple, direct proof that it belongs to catalytic logspace CL, where CL means CSPACE(O(log n), n^{O(1)}), i.e. deterministic computation with O(log n) ordinary workspace plus polynomially many catalytic bits that must be restored exactly on halting?

evidence.quote: Definition 3. The class CL is defined as CSPACE(O(log n), nO(1)).
Problem 2. Give a simple, direct proof of uSTConn ∈ CL.

accepted.question_text: Does the directed s-t connectivity problem admit a simple, direct proof that it belongs to catalytic logspace CL?

evidence.quote: Problem 3. Give a simple, direct proof of STConn ∈ CL.

accepted.question_text: Can Savitch’s theorem be improved by proving that every nondeterministic space-s computation can be simulated in deterministic space o(s^2), rather than only the known O(s^2) bound?

evidence.quote: Savitch’s Theorem [Sav70], which states that NSPACE(s) ⊆ SPACE(O(s2)), is one of the bedrocks of space complexity, but it is not known to be tight.
Problem 4. Try to improve Savitch’s Theorem: prove NSPACE(s) ⊆ SPACE(o(s2)).

accepted.question_text: Can the best known deterministic space upper bound for randomized space BPSPACE(s) be improved?

evidence.quote: Problem 5. Improve the deterministic space complexity of BPSPACE(s).

accepted.question_text: What is the true space complexity of the Tree Evaluation Problem, where the input is a rooted full binary tree of height h whose leaves carry values in [k] and whose internal nodes are labeled by functions from [k] × [k] to [k], and the task is to evaluate the root?

evidence.quote: The function is defined, for an alphabet size k and height h, by a height h rooted full binary tree, where leaves are given values in [k] and internal nodes are labeled
with functions from [k] × [k] to [k].
Problem 6. Decide the space complexity of TreeEval.

accepted.question_text: Is there a register program that, for every polynomial p(x1, ..., xn), uses only O(n) registers over a constant-size ring and only O(1) recursive calls to the multiplication subprogram Px, where Px adds x1 ··· xn to the designated registers, and thereby computes p efficiently enough to support the desired TreeEval applications?

evidence.quote: Definition 4. A register program P with space s := s(n) and time t := t(n) is comprised of a set of s blocks of memory, or what we will call registers, R1 . . .Rs

Problem 7. Give a register program for computing any polynomial p(x1 . . . xn) using O(n) registers over a constant size ring R and O(1) recursive calls to program Px, whose effect is to add x1 . . . xn to R1 . . .Rn respectively.

accepted.question_text: For every sufficiently wide branching program of width w = Ω(1) and length ℓ, is there an equivalent branching program of width w/2 and length O(ℓ)?

evidence.quote: Problem 8. Show that for any branching program B of sufficiently large width w = Ω (1) and length ℓ, there exists a branching program B ′ of width w /2 and length O(ℓ) computing the same function.

accepted.question_text: For every sufficiently wide branching program of width w and length ℓ, is there an equivalent branching program of width w − 1 and length poly(ℓ)?

evidence.quote: Problem 9. Show that for any branching program B of sufficiently large width w and length ℓ, there exists a branching program B ′ of width w − 1 and length poly (ℓ) computing the same function.

accepted.question_text: Is there any function whose best known or optimal algorithm really needs space s in the ordinary model SPACE(s), but can be computed using almost entirely catalytic memory in the sense of belonging to CSPACE(≪ s, ≈ s), with only a much smaller ordinary work tape and nearly all memory coming from restorable catalytic space?

evidence.quote: Definition 2. The class CSPACE(s, c) is the set of all functions which can be computed by a catalytic Turing Machine which has space s and catalytic space c.

Problem 10. Find any function whose optimal space algorithm can be made almost entirely catalytic, i.e. a function requiring—or even that we only know how to do in— SPACE(s) but which is computable in CSPACE(≪ s, ≈ s).

accepted.question_text: Can every catalytic logspace computation be simulated in polynomial time; equivalently, is CL ⊆ P?

evidence.quote: Definition 3. The class CL is defined as CSPACE(O(log n), nO(1)).
Problem 11. Prove CL ⊆ P.

accepted.question_text: Can one prove that if L is a strict subset of P, then catalytic logspace CL is still contained in P?
accepted.context_brief: conditional containment of CL in P

evidence.quote: Problem 12. Show that L ⊊ P implies CL ⊆ P.

accepted.question_text: Can one show that proving CL ⊆ P would already provide strong evidence that ZPP ⊆ P?

evidence.quote: Problem 13. Show that CL ⊆ P would give strong evidence ZPP ⊆ P.

accepted.question_text: Can catalytic logspace compute every NC2 circuit, or at least every circuit of depth ω(log n)?
accepted.context_brief: beyond logarithmic circuit depth in CL

evidence.quote: Problem 14. Show that NC2, or even any circuit of ω(log n) depth, can be computed in CL.

accepted.question_text: Is there a register program that computes x^k in the non-commutative setting using only linear space and a constant number of recursive calls to x?

evidence.quote: Problem 15. Give a register program for computing x k in the non-commutative setting using linear space and a constant number of recursive calls to x.

accepted.question_text: Can randomized NC1 with read-multiple randomness, denoted BPNC1, be simulated in catalytic logspace CL?

evidence.quote: Problem 16. Show that BPNC1 ⊆ CL.

accepted.question_text: For every Boolean function f on n input bits, can one design a catalytic branching program with 2^{O(n)} possible start nodes and total size 2^{O(n)} · O(n) that computes f while restoring the initial catalytic state?

evidence.quote: Girard et al. [GKM15] define catalytic branching programs in the following way: rather than having a single start node ... we have m different start nodes ... The catalytic property ... states that on input x, each start node τ must reach exactly the end node labeled with f (x) and τ.
Problem 17. Design a catalytic branching program with 2O(n) start nodes and total size 2O(n) · O(n) for any function f .

accepted.question_text: What is the computational power of the advice class CL/poly, and is there a natural syntactic characterization of it?

evidence.quote: Problem 18. What is the power of CL/poly, and does it have a natural syntactic characterization?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an oracle D relative to which catalytic logspace becomes as powerful as EXP; that is, can one show CL^D = EXP^D?

evidence.quote: Problem 19. Show the existence of an oracle D such that CLD = EXPD.

accepted.question_text: Can the known inclusion BPL ⊆ CL be extended to the catalytic randomized class CBPL, proving CBPL ⊆ CL?

evidence.quote: The randomized class CBPL was introduced by Datta et al. [DGJ +20]
Problem 20. Extend the BPL ⊆ CL simulation to show CBPL ⊆ CL.

accepted.question_text: Is catalytic logspace robust to small restoration errors on the catalytic tape, in the sense that allowing either ω(1) final errors or merely an expected O(1) number of final errors still yields the same class CL?

evidence.quote: Problem 21. Show that CL is equivalent even if we allowω(1) many errors on the catalytic tape at the end, or alternatively if we allow Ex,τ[O(1)] many such errors.

accepted.question_text: Can nondeterminism be used together with catalytic computation in a genuinely nontrivial way, rather than merely by definition?

evidence.quote: Problem 22. Utilize non-determinism in conjunction with catalytic computing in a non-trivial way.

accepted.question_text: Can one prove a catalytic analogue of Savitch’s theorem by showing that every nondeterministic catalytic computation using work space s and catalytic space c can be simulated deterministically in catalytic space (s^2, c^2), that is, CNSPACE(s, c) ⊆ CSPACE(s^2, c^2)?

evidence.quote: Problem 23. Prove CNSPACE(s, c) ⊆ CSPACE(s2, c2).

accepted.question_text: Can one implement a catalytic algorithm that is genuinely useful in practice, rather than only of theoretical interest?

evidence.quote: Problem 24. Implement a catalytic algorithm such that it is actually useful.

accepted.question_text: What should the right notion of quantum catalytic space be?

evidence.quote: Problem 25. What does quantum catalytic space look like?

accepted.question_text: Can one devise a register-program model based on elementary operations inspired by unitary quantum computation and use it to prove nontrivial consequences, for example for BQP?

evidence.quote: Problem 26. Devise a register program using basic instructions inspired by unitary computation, and use it to show non-trivial results for e.g. BQP.

accepted.question_text: Can one devise a circuit that uses techniques from space reuse or catalytic computing to solve some problem efficiently in a way that is not currently known directly in the circuit model?

evidence.quote: Problem 27. Devise a circuit that uses techniques from space reuse and catalytic computing to solve some problem in low size or depth in a way that we do not know how to do directly.

accepted.question_text: Can one prove that the threshold-circuit class TC1 is contained in the arithmetic-circuit class VP?

evidence.quote: Problem 28. Show TC1 ⊆ VP.

accepted.question_text: For an undirected capacitated network with designated source-sink pairs, is the network coding conjecture true or false; that is, can coding or mixing messages ever beat the throughput permitted by ordinary multicommodity flow?

evidence.quote: In essence, the question is whether or not, for a given undirected graph with capacities on each edge and a set of source-sink pairs, we can send more message bits from each source to its corresponding sink than the network flow should allow if we think of the messages as being generic commodities instead.
Problem 29. Is the network coding conjecture true or false?

accepted.question_text: If every node in the network is restricted to sending only linear transformations of its incoming messages, can one prove or disprove the network coding conjecture under that restriction?

evidence.quote: Problem 30. Prove or disprove the network coding conjecture when all nodes are restricted to sending linear transformations of their incoming messages.

accepted.question_text: Is there a meaningful notion of a catalytic data structure, or any genuine benefit to storing a data structure in catalytic memory that must be restored after use?

evidence.quote: Problem 31. Is there a meaningful notion of a catalytic data structure, or is there anything to be gained from a data structure stored in catalytic memory?

accepted.question_text: Under a believable cryptographic assumption, can one show that catalytic logspace CL is contained in some plausible subclass of P, perhaps even NC?

evidence.quote: Problem 32. Show CL is contained in some subclass of P, perhaps NC, given a believable cryptographic assumption.

accepted.question_text: Can techniques based on reusing space be turned into evidence against natural cryptographic objects or primitives?

evidence.quote: Problem 33. Show evidence against objects in cryptography based on techniques in reusing space.

accepted.question_text: Can clean computation, where the evolving memory state reveals no secrets about the computed function at any single time step, be used to obtain a natural class of cryptographic objects, either conditionally or unconditionally?

evidence.quote: In other words, our memory at every point in time reveals no secrets about the computation of f .
Problem 34. Show the existence, conditional or otherwise, of a natural class of cryptographic objects by using clean computation.

accepted.question_text: Can one prove that if one-way functions exist in catalytic logspace CL, or even if some one-way function is computable by a polynomial-size polynomial-length register program, then one-way functions already exist in NC0?
accepted.context_brief: one-way functions from CL to NC0

evidence.quote: Problem 35. Prove that the existence of one-way functions in CL, or even any one-way function computable by a poly-size poly-length register program, implies the existence of one-way functions in NC0.

trace.notes: Normalized the zbMATH URL as a resolver record and recovered the exact full-text PDF from the linked Bulletin of EATCS article.
Mapped the PDF structure; Part II on pages 26-42 contains the open-problem material, with a master list on pages 27-28 and detailed discussions on pages 29-42.
Extracted all 35 explicitly numbered open problems from the survey's master list and detailed problem sections.

Expanded source-specific terminology such as catalytic Turing machine, CSPACE, CL, and catalytic branching programs using the survey's earlier definitions so the rewritten questions are self-contained.
Expanded compressed problem statements using nearby definitional text for TreeEval, register programs, the network coding conjecture, and clean computation.
No duplicate questions were merged; the source presents 35 distinct numbered problems.
All 35 items passed self-containedness, evidence, and no-new-facts checks against the readable PDF, so no item was moved to needs_review.
Saved the exact JSON payload to outputs/parse-paper/reusing-space-techniques-and-open-problems.json and updated outputs/latest.json.
